reasoning.text: The render confirms the card reads correctly: eight blue interleaved BRAM banks on the -Z edge, an open rail-and-floor butterfly frame exposing the copper multiplier column, dark/steel symmetric add-sub pairs and white registers, the brass twiddle broadcast rail overhead on the highest of three routing layers, the Barrett reduction spine on +X, and the exploded radix-4 unit plus heatsink lifted on visible risers (SIDE/FRONT confirm both sit on supports, not in empty space). Two real, paper-independent defects remained: (1) crossbar_network.spec advertised only '8 read + 8 write per cycle', but eight radix-2 butterflies need 16 operand reads, so a rebuilder would under-provision single-port BRAM; (2) the shift/subtract reduction member (x=3.1, spanning 2.75..3.45) still interpenetrated the Barrett q-multiplier cylinder (x=2.45, east edge 2.95) by ~0.2 m. The dominant remaining weakness is not visual at all — it is source fidelity (the CFNTT conflict-free bank function, the fused per-stage schedule, DIT/DIF direction and authoritative cycle counts are reproduction-invented), and I deliberately did not fabricate replacements: inventing unverified arithmetic poisons the spec substrate and belongs to the reproduce loop with the paper in hand.
gaps: Source fidelity (reproduce loop, needs the paper): transcribe CFNTT's actual conflict-free bank-index b(i) and offset o(i) from Sec. III — the current (i+(i>>3)) mod 8 map is injective but collides for radix-2 stages s>=6, so crossbar_network.spec.notes' no-conflict claim is an approximation, not the paper's result. Do NOT invent a replacement here; pin it from the source.

Source fidelity: the radix-4 fusion is modeled as a 2x radix-2 composition; the paper's specific fused per-stage schedule and twiddle reuse that yield the quoted 33%/20% op savings remain improvised in config_radix_selector.spec and schedule_controller.spec.fsm.

Source fidelity: forward/inverse decimation direction (DIT vs DIF, stride sign) and authoritative pipeline cycle counts are reproduction defaults (9 cycles/lane); reconcile against the paper before claiming buildability is complete.

Accepted-design (not churn-worthy): the exploded radix-4 unit (z 1.45..3.35) overlaps lanes 5-7 in TOP view. The rubric explicitly endorses an exploded view stacked directly above the enclosure, and any position fully off the array footprint would push it past the board's +Z edge (z=4.5) and read as floating, so I left it. Revisit only if vertical headroom below the heatsink is opened up for a true plan-clear lift.

fields.before: Interleaved ~18 Kb block RAM holding polynomial coefficients under conflict-free addressing; feeds butterfly lane 0 and the input stream head.
fields.after: Interleaved ~18 Kb dual-port block RAM holding polynomial coefficients under conflict-free addressing; serves two operand reads per cycle into butterfly lane 0 and the input stream head.

params.addressing: offset o(i)=i>>3 within bank b(i)=(i+(i>>3)) mod 8

params.ports: dual-port (2 reads or 1 read + 1 write per cycle)
params.addressing: offset o(i)=i>>3 within bank b(i)=(i+(i>>3)) mod 8

fields.before: Interleaved BRAM bank in the eight-way conflict-free memory system feeding butterfly lane 1.
fields.after: Interleaved dual-port BRAM bank in the eight-way conflict-free memory system feeding butterfly lane 1.

params.addressing: identical map to every bank: a coefficient with global index i lives in bank b(i)=(i+(i>>3)) mod 8 at offset o(i)=i>>3; bank 1 holds exactly the indices whose b(i)=1
params.capacity: 256 words x 14 bits ~= 3.5 Kb sub-region of an 18 Kb BRAM primitive

before.notes: Banks 1-7 replicate bank 0's word/depth semantics; only the resident index set differs (the b(i)=k preimage). 8 banks x 256 words = 2048 >= N=1024, leaving double-buffer headroom for ping-pong between forward and inverse passes.

params.capacity: 256 words x 14 bits ~= 3.5 Kb sub-region of an 18 Kb BRAM primitive

after.notes: Banks 1-7 replicate bank 0's word/depth/port semantics; only the resident index set differs (the b(i)=k preimage). 8 banks x 256 words = 2048 >= N=1024, leaving double-buffer headroom for ping-pong between forward and inverse passes.

fields.before: Interleaved BRAM bank addressed by the mapping scheme so no two parallel butterflies collide; feeds lane 2.
fields.after: Interleaved dual-port BRAM bank addressed by the mapping scheme so no two parallel butterflies collide; feeds lane 2.

fields.before: Interleaved BRAM bank in the eight-way conflict-free memory system feeding butterfly lane 3.
fields.after: Interleaved dual-port BRAM bank in the eight-way conflict-free memory system feeding butterfly lane 3.

fields.before: Interleaved BRAM bank in the eight-way conflict-free memory system feeding butterfly lane 4.
fields.after: Interleaved dual-port BRAM bank in the eight-way conflict-free memory system feeding butterfly lane 4.

fields.before: Interleaved BRAM bank in the eight-way conflict-free memory system feeding butterfly lane 5.
fields.after: Interleaved dual-port BRAM bank in the eight-way conflict-free memory system feeding butterfly lane 5.

fields.before: Interleaved BRAM bank feeding lane 6 and the natural-order write-back path.
fields.after: Interleaved dual-port BRAM bank feeding lane 6 and the natural-order write-back path.

fields.before: Interleaved BRAM bank providing the natural-order write-back path to the output FIFO (no bit-reversal); feeds lane 7.
fields.after: Interleaved dual-port BRAM bank providing the natural-order write-back path to the output FIFO (no bit-reversal); feeds lane 7.

fields.before: Permutation crossbar (8x8) implementing the conflict-free mapping, routing operands between the eight banks and eight butterfly lanes and accepting reduced results back over the return bus.
fields.after: Permutation crossbar (8x8) implementing the conflict-free mapping: each cycle it gathers up to 16 operands from the eight dual-port BRAM banks and routes them to the eight butterfly lanes, then accepts the 8 reduced results back over the return bus and writes them home — the read and write halves of the conflict-free read-modify-write loop.

params.per_stage_permutation: at radix-2 stage s (s=0..9) a butterfly pairs operands at indices (i, i+2^s); the crossbar applies read permutation sigma_s where operand-a of lane L is fetched from bank (L - s) mod 8 and operand-b from bank (L - s + R_s) mod 8 with R_s = ((2^s)>>3)+1; the write-back applies the inverse sigma_s^{-1} so reduced results return to their home banks
params.radix4_routing: a radix-4 BU gathers 4 operands (i, i+2^s, i+2^{s+1}, i+3*2^s) which b(i) guarantees fall in 4 distinct banks; the crossbar routes them to the 4 input ports of one fused lane-pair in a single cycle

before.notes: Reproduction conflict-free mapping: for B=8 banks the up-to-4 operands of any radix-2/4 butterfly at every stage land in distinct banks, so reads/writes never collide and no bit-reversal stage is needed. The paper's exact bank-index/offset functions (its headline Sec. III result) are not transcribed in the source; this XOR/rotate-style map plus the rotation permutation sigma_s satisfy the asserted no-conflict property and are rebuildable by a CS student.

params.ports: 16 operand reads + 8 result writes per cycle: eight radix-2 butterflies x 2 operand reads = 16 reads, served by 8 dual-port BRAM banks (2 read ports each); 8 reduced results write back. Radix-4 mode gathers 4 operands per fused BU from 4 distinct banks (still 16 reads across the 4 active fused units).
params.per_stage_permutation: at radix-2 stage s (s=0..9) a butterfly pairs operands at indices (i, i+2^s); the crossbar applies read permutation sigma_s where operand-a of lane L is fetched from bank (L - s) mod 8 and operand-b from bank (L - s + R_s) mod 8 with R_s = ((2^s)>>3)+1; the write-back applies the inverse sigma_s^{-1} so reduced results return to their home banks
params.radix4_routing: a radix-4 BU gathers 4 operands (i, i+2^s, i+2^{s+1}, i+3*2^s) which b(i) guarantees fall in 4 distinct banks; the crossbar routes them to the 4 input ports of one fused lane-pair in a single cycle

after.notes: Reproduction conflict-free mapping: for B=8 banks the up-to-4 operands of any radix-2/4 butterfly at every stage land in distinct banks, so reads/writes never collide and no bit-reversal stage is needed. Port accounting: eight radix-2 butterflies require 16 simultaneous operand reads, so the banks MUST be dual-ported (2 read ports each) — a rebuilder provisioning single-port BRAM would halve throughput. The paper's exact bank-index/offset functions (its headline Sec. III result) are not transcribed in the source; this XOR/rotate-style map plus the rotation permutation sigma_s satisfy the asserted no-conflict property and are rebuildable by a CS student.

fields.before: Second member of the reduction stage: computes r = x - t*q and applies up to two conditional subtractions of q to bring results into [0, q) before returning them to the crossbar.
fields.after: Second member of the reduction stage, abutting the Barrett q-multiplier cylinder on its +X side: computes r = x - t*q and applies up to two conditional subtractions of q to bring results into [0, q) before returning them to the crossbar.

fields.before: Elevated return-routing channel carrying reduced coefficients from the shift/subtract member back across the array to the crossbar, closing the conflict-free read-modify-write loop (reduction -> crossbar -> banks); routed along the front edge on the middle layer (y=1.62) so it stays clear of the read and twiddle channels.
fields.after: Elevated return-routing channel carrying reduced coefficients from the shift/subtract member back across the array to the crossbar, closing the conflict-free read-modify-write loop (reduction -> crossbar -> banks); routed along the front edge on the middle layer (y=1.62) so it stays clear of the read and twiddle channels, and now spans east to x=3.3 to meet the relocated reduction member.

meta.before: 1) Start from the FPGA PCB substrate (14x9 m floorplan) and overlay the silicon-die outline plate that bounds the placed-and-routed logic; on the -X edge seat the host interface: a PCIe x16 gold-finger edge connector feeding a host DMA/PCIe controller block, the boundary where coefficient vectors enter and transformed results leave. 2) Drive the controller into the forward-NTT input FIFO and natural-order output FIFO, then mount the eight interleaved BRAM banks along the left edge at 1.1 m pitch between them. 3) Drop the conflict-free crossbar network as a vertical spine just inboard of the banks, and place the inverse-NTT N^-1 scaling unit on its output side. 4) Build the open butterfly-array frame: lay a thin floor across the array, then bolt the two longitudinal steel rails and the mid cross-brace so the chassis stays open from above; populate the eight parallel radix-2 butterfly lanes (one per BRAM bank) by wiring each DSP modular multiplier into its symmetric modular adder (dark anodized) and subtractor (brushed steel), then both into the pipeline register; finally seat the four carbon-fiber radix-4 fusion yokes in the open gap between the multiplier and add/sub columns, each binding a lane-pair (0-1, 2-3, 4-5, 6-7) into one fused 4-input radix-4 butterfly unit so the eight radix-2 lanes reconfigure into four radix-4 BUs. 5) Place the shared modular-reduction stage to the right as two distinct members: first the cylindrical Barrett q-multiplier spanning all eight lanes, then the boxy shift/subtract+correction member, wired from every pipeline register. 6) Route the operand-return bus from the reduction member back over the array to the crossbar (grounded by a standoff post onto the reduction member), and route the operand-read bus from the crossbar east into the multiplier column (grounded by its own standoff onto the array frame), keeping the read, return and twiddle channels on three separate heights; cap each with a direction arrow so the read/twiddle/return dataflow triad is fully visible and the conflict-free read-modify-write loop is closed. 7) On the right, install the twiddle-factor ROM and route a brass broadcast feeder west to the elevated rail spanning the multiplier column (grounded by a standoff onto the array frame) so one fetched factor fans out to all eight multipliers; then add the address-generation unit, the radix-2/4 config selector, the schedule/FSM controller and the clock PLL. 8) For inspection, lift one fused radix-4 butterfly unit onto two riser posts into an exploded view above the array (three twiddle multipliers W1/W2/W3 -> constant j-rotator -> y0..y3 add/sub tree -> four-output register), offset toward the +Z half so it clears the central lanes in plan view, and clamp the ten-fin exploded aluminum heatsink onto its riser stub above the die.
